title: feat(net): restore rcon next to the management protocol
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

RCON was replaced by the server management protocol in 34a85ae94. MSMP cannot run arbitrary commands, so admin tools, `rcon-cli` style scripts and automated tests lost their command channel. This brings RCON back next to MSMP with the code as it was before that commit: `networking.rcon` in the config, off by default, no start with an empty password, and commands run with console permissions (owner level, like vanilla `RconConsoleSource`).

The second commit sends a command's output as one response, split into 4096-byte fragments like vanilla `RconClient.sendCmdResponse`. The old handler sent one packet per output line, so a client that reads one response per command got the leftover lines as the answer to its next command. Lines are joined with `\n` (vanilla `RconConsoleSource.sendSystemMessage` appends them without a separator), and the split is by bytes on char boundaries where vanilla counts UTF-16 chars.

- feat(net): restore rcon next to the management protocol
- fix(rcon): send the command output as one response like vanilla (4096-byte fragments)

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- Unit tests `short_output_is_one_response` and `long_output_is_split_on_char_boundaries` (6000 bytes of `ü` become two fragments of at most 4096 bytes that concatenate back to the input).
- All mineflayer bot specs of the BedWars project (combined branch) do their setup over RCON (`tp`, `give`, `data get entity ...`) with a client that reads one response per command. Before the second commit, `data get entity X` there returned the second line of an earlier `/bw list`.
- Not checked: nothing fires `RemoteServerCommandEvent` (it comes back as a type; the RCON handler did not fire it before the removal either), and the rcon fuzz target removed in 34a85ae94 is not restored.
- No in-game effect. With an RCON client: enable `networking.rcon` with a password, run a command with several output lines, expect them in one response.

title: fix(protocol): read a zero LpVec3 as the single byte vanilla writes
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

A mineflayer 26.1 bot that right-clicks any entity is kicked with "Error while handling incoming packet incomplete". Vanilla `LpVec3.read` (and Pumpkin's own `LpVector3d::write`) encode the zero vector as a single `0x00` byte, but `LpVector3d::read` read two bytes before it checked for zero, so it consumed the next field too. `ServerboundInteractPacket` ends with the `LpVec3` hit position and the sneaking bool, so a zero hit position failed with `failed to fill whole buffer`. The read now looks at the first byte alone, like `LpVec3.read`.

Upstream #4308 fixes the same bug the same way; this was found independently.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- `zero_vector_is_one_byte_and_reads_back_without_consuming_more`: the zero vector writes `[0x00]`, and reading `[0x00, 0x01]` returns zero and leaves the `0x01` unread (fails on master). `non_zero_vector_round_trips` checks that a normal vector still round trips.
- `30-shop.test.js` and `98-net-sync.test.js` (combined branch) open the shop by right-clicking a villager with a mineflayer bot through ViaProxy, which kicked the bot before.
- Not checked: no real-client capture; a real client only runs into this when it sends a zero hit position.
- In game: right-click an entity with a client that sends a zero hit position (e.g. a mineflayer 26.1 bot), expect no kick.

title: feat(combat): optional Minecraft 1.8 combat for modern clients
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Adds `[pvp.legacy_combat]` (off by default), which gives 26.x clients 1.8 PvP the way the OldCombatMechanics plugin does on Paper: no attack cooldown (attack speed 40), 1.8 weapon damage, Sharpness, criticals (sprinting allowed), Strength and Weakness, 1.8 knockback, armour and Protection with the 1.8 random roll, sword blocking, 1.8 natural regeneration and the 1.8 bow launch (speed, Gaussian spread, no shooter movement). A plugin can't do this today: `Player::attack` ignores the `attack_speed` attribute, and a player's server velocity is never ticked, so knockback has no usable input. Punch only pushes after a hit that did damage (legacy mode only).

Commits in order:
- the combat rules and config (`entity/legacy_combat.rs`). One part applies to all modes: the hurt cooldown now compares raw damage with raw damage and applies armour only to what gets through, like vanilla `LivingEntity.hurtServer` / `actuallyHurt`. Before, a stronger second hit inside the cooldown could be dropped when the victim wore armour.
- 1.8 attack distance: attacks from 6 blocks or more (feet to feet) are ignored.
- knockback starts from a server copy of the player's motion that only decays, sees jumps and is restored after a melee hit, like 1.8. Before, it used the client's motion, which still held the last knockback, so a few hits in a row sent the victim flying.
- arrows start on the look ray (0.1 below the eyes) instead of 1.8's 0.16 to the right, which looked off centre with a 26.x crosshair. Speed, spread and flight stay 1.8.
- a stuck arrow stops 0.05 back along its motion, like 1.8. 26.3 (and Pumpkin) use the sign of each axis, which leaves a flat shot 0.05 above the floor (1.8.9 measured 0.007).

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- Unit tests in `legacy_combat.rs`: weapon damage table, damage order (crit only on the base, Sharpness added after), crit conditions, base and extra knockback, armour and Protection rolls, sword blocking, arrow launch, and vertical knockback on a jumping player against what a real 1.8.9 server sent (0.4 while rising, 0.322 eight ticks after the jump, 0.361 standing).
- Bot spec `50-melee.test.js` on the combined branch: no cooldown UI, damage and crits, 10 tick hit delay (a stronger hit deals only the difference), reach (3.0 hits, 7.0 ignored), knockback 0.4 / sprint 0.9 / Knockback I 0.9, three hits in a row 0.4 each (1.8.9: 0.4 / 0.4 / 0.4), sword blocking (5 to 3.0), armour, regeneration about every 4 s.
- Bot spec `40-bow.test.js`: launch speed 3.0, 1.8 spread, origin on the look ray, no shooter movement. Against a real 1.8.9 server (128 identical shots, before the look ray change): launch speed 2.9965 on 1.8.9 and 2.9972 here, spread per axis 0.0073 and 0.0076, same spawn offset.
- Not checked: the hurt cooldown change in vanilla combat mode (the specs run with legacy combat on), Bedrock clients.
- In game: set `[pvp.legacy_combat] enabled = true`, hit a player with quick sword clicks, expect no cooldown indicator, full damage every 10 ticks and the same 0.4 knockback on every hit. Block with a sword the client can use (e.g. one with a `consumable` component), expect (damage + 1) / 2.

title: feat(plugin): drop-item, get-entity-by-id and run-command for wasm
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

The v0.1 plugin API had no way to drop an item stack into the world, to get an entity from the ids that events carry, or to run a console command and read what it printed. A BedWars plugin needs all three (resource spawners, event handlers, `difficulty normal` at load). This adds `world.drop-item(pos, item, velocity, pickup-delay, can-merge)`, `world.get-entity-by-id(id)` (players included) and `server.run-command(cmd) -> list<string>`, which runs the command with console permissions through a `CommandSender::Rcon` that collects the output. Without a velocity the drop gets the random spread of vanilla `Block.popResource`. With `can-merge` false the item entity never merges, through a flag checked in `ItemEntity::is_mergeable` (vanilla `ItemEntity.isMergable`); cancelling `item-merge-event` instead costs one Wasm call per candidate pair.

Builds on {{PR:feat/rcon}} (`run-command` collects the output through its `CommandSender::Rcon`), whose commits are included here; the change of this PR is the last 2 commits.

Commits:
1. feat(plugin): drop-item, get-entity-by-id and run-command for wasm plugins
2. feat(plugin): drop-item can spawn item entities that never merge

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- `tests/specs/20-economy.test.js` on the combined branch: the spawners drop through `drop-item` with `can-merge` false. The spec checks that every drop lands on a spawner of its type with the right item and name, that the server's ground items match what the clients saw spawn, and that bronze stays one entity per drop.
- Not checked: the branch on its own; the specs and the play test ran on the combined branch.
- In game: drop two equal stacks next to each other with `can-merge` false, expect two item entities that stay apart and can both be picked up.

title: feat(world): filtered explosions, explosion knockback via the packet
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

A BedWars TNT may only break blocks that players placed, and the map has to stay. The new `world.explode-filtered(pos, power, breakable, entity-damage, exempt-entities)` runs a TNT-like explosion (vanilla rays, blast resistance, damage and knockback) through a `FilteredExplosionCalculator` that only lets the listed blocks explode, can replace the entity damage with a fixed value, spares the listed entities and returns the blocks it destroyed. It does not fire `EntityExplodeEvent`, since the plugin is the caller.

The same commit fixes explosion knockback for players. `Explosion::damage_entities` called `add_velocity` on players too, which sent an absolute velocity built from the stale server-side motion plus the push. Like vanilla (`ServerExplosion.hurtEntities` collects `hitPlayers`, `ServerLevel.explode` sends them as `ClientboundExplodePacket.playerKnockback`), the push now goes in the explosion packet and the client adds it to its own motion.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- `tests/specs/60-special-items.test.js` on the combined branch: the shop TNT explodes through `explode-filtered` with the placer exempt. The spec checks that it hurts the enemy next to it, does not hurt the placer, and that the island floor survives.
- Not checked: the branch on its own; the player knockback from the packet has no bot check and no real-client capture.
- In game: stand a few blocks from TNT, expect to be pushed away like on vanilla (also while running), with no snap to an old motion. With `explode-filtered`, expect only the listed blocks to break.

title: feat(plugin): close-screen, sync-inventory and shareable GUIs for wasm
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Plugins could not close a player's screen, resend the inventory after cancelling a click, or show one GUI to several players: `open-gui` consumes its handle, so a team chest could only be opened once. This adds `player.close-screen()` (`Player::close_handled_screen`, vanilla `ServerPlayer.closeContainer`), `player.sync-inventory()` (`Player::sync_inventory_to_client`) and `gui.share()`, which returns a new handle with the same title and settings around the same `Arc<PluginInventory>`, so every viewer sees the same items. `close-screen` runs through `pump_blocking`: closing fires `InventoryCloseEvent`, and as a plain sync import it froze the server when the same plugin listened to that event (the tick thread waited for the store that was busy with the call), with nothing in the log.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- `tests/specs/60-special-items.test.js` on the combined branch: the team chest opens shares of one GUI. The spec checks that a teammate sees the items the placer put in and an enemy does not.
- `tests/specs/30-shop.test.js` on the combined branch: a refused purchase cancels the click and calls `sync-inventory`; the spec checks that the inventory is unchanged afterwards.
- Not checked: the branch on its own; the specs and the play test ran on the combined branch.
- In game: open a GUI for one player and its share for another, put an item in on one side, expect it on the other. Call `close-screen` from a plugin that listens to `inventory-close-event`, expect the screen to close and the server to keep ticking.

title: fix(plugin): resolve WIT sounds by name instead of the enum Debug text
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Every `player.play-sound`, `player.play-sound-at` and `world.play-sound` call trapped in the v0.1 and v0.2 hosts. The host built the sound id with `format!("{sound:?}").to_lowercase().replace('_', ".")`, but `Debug` gives `UiButtonClick`, so the lookup was `uibuttonclick` and never matched. The trap stops the plugin's store driver, so after the first sound every later event and task of that plugin failed. A shared helper in `pumpkin-wasm-host-common` now matches the variant name against `Sound::NAMES`, with both sides reduced to lowercase letters and digits.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- Unit test `sound::tests::variant_names_find_vanilla_sounds`: a plain variant, `Debug` text with a `Sound::` prefix and a long name (`EntityAllayAmbientWithItem`) find their vanilla sound, an unknown name gives `None`.
- Not checked: the branch on its own; no bot spec checks a plugin sound.
- In game: play `ui-button-click` to a player from a Wasm plugin, expect the click and no "Wasm plugin store driver stopped" in the log.

title: feat(plugin): force chunk loading and loaded checks for wasm plugins
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Block reads in unloaded chunks return air and writes are lost, so a plugin that inspects or edits an area without players nearby fails silently (BedWars on a map whose lobby is 380 blocks from the beds: no bed found at round start, no shops, no drops). `/forceload` cannot help for plugin-created worlds, which all use the dimension name `minecraft:overworld` and cannot be targeted by commands. This adds `world.set-chunks-forced(corner-a, corner-b, forced)` and `world.is-chunk-loaded(chunk-x, chunk-z)`. Besides `World::forced_chunks`, which only marks chunks as simulated, it adds a force ticket for each newly forced chunk and removes it on release, like the `TicketType.FORCED` ticket of vanilla `ServerLevel.setChunkForced`. Loading stays asynchronous, so the plugin polls `is-chunk-loaded`.

The `/forceload` command has the same missing ticket and is left unchanged here.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- `tests/specs/03-map-mansion.test.js` (through `map-smoke.js`) on the combined branch: the plugin forces the arena chunks at load and waits for them. The spec checks the beds at their configured positions, the shop villagers and the spawner drops on the Mansion map.
- Not checked: the branch on its own; the specs and the play test ran on the combined branch.
- In game: force an area far from every player, wait until `is-chunk-loaded` is true, set a block there, fly over, expect the block.

title: feat(plugin): entity explode event carries the source entity and world
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

`World::run_explosion` fired `EntityExplodeEvent` with entity id 0 for every explosion, and the event had no world, so a plugin could not tell whose explosion it was or where it happened. TNT, creepers, end crystals, TNT minecarts, fireballs and the wither now pass their entity id through the new `World::explode_from`, as vanilla passes the source entity to `Level.explode` (for example `Creeper.explodeCreeper`, `PrimedTnt.explode`). The event gets a `world` field and the v0.1 WIT record `entity-explode-event-data` gets `world-name`. Explosions without a source (`World::explode`, `explode_with_calculator`) keep id 0.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- `tests/specs/60-special-items.test.js` on the combined branch: the plugin cancels every vanilla explosion and redoes it in the arena it finds by `world-name`, so the TNT control check (a summoned vanilla TNT hurts the player next to it) only passes when the world is right.
- Not checked: the branch on its own; the v0.2 WIT record is unchanged.
- No in-game change without a plugin that listens to `entity-explode-event`.

title: fix(player): move the chunk view when the server teleports a player
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

After a server teleport (`/tp`, a plugin teleport, a respawn at a far spawn point) a player who stands still gets no chunks at the target until its next position packet. A real client sends one at the latest every 20 ticks, a bot possibly never, so the player can fall into the void meanwhile. `Player::request_teleport` set the position but left `chunker::update_position` to `handle_position`. The teleport now updates the chunk view right away. In vanilla the position is set in `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.teleport` and `ChunkMap.tick` runs `updateChunkTracking` for every player each tick, so the view follows without a client packet.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- No unit test: the change is a call into the existing chunker.
- Not checked: only checked on the combined branch, no real-client capture.
- In game: `/tp` a player who stands still to a far, unloaded area, expect the terrain to load at once and the player not to fall.

title: fix(net): ignore confirms of superseded teleports like vanilla
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Two teleports in quick succession (for example a world change followed by a plugin teleport) kicked the client with "Wrong teleport id" as soon as it confirmed the first one. The client confirms every teleport it gets, so a confirm for an older id is normal. Vanilla `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleAcceptTeleportPacket` only acts on the id it awaits and ignores the others; Pumpkin now does the same. A confirm while no teleport is awaited still kicks. This was also why a teleport from a plugin's join handler kicked the joining player.

Upstream #3466 fixes the same kick and also serializes the teleport id, the awaited teleport and the packet; that part is in {{PR:fix/teleport-id-lock}}.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- Not checked: no bot spec targets this directly; only checked on the combined branch.
- In game: have a plugin teleport a player right after moving it to another world (or from the join handler), expect no "Wrong teleport id" kick and the player at the second target.

title: fix(projectile): thrown items, tridents, hooks and fangs can hit players
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Snowballs, eggs, ender pearls and the other thrown items, tridents, fishing hooks and evoker fangs flew through players. They collected their targets with `World::get_entities_at_box`, which by its doc comment returns only non-player entities. They now use `get_all_at_box` (splash potions, fireworks and shulker bullets add players by hand and were not affected). Since players can be hit now, thrown items, tridents and fishing hooks skip spectators, like vanilla `Projectile.canHitEntity` (`Entity.canBeHitByProjectile` is false for spectators through `Player.isPickable`).
Arrows had the same lookup; that part is in {{PR:fix/arrow-flight-order}}.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- No unit test added. No bot spec covers these projectiles: the BedWars specs only shoot arrows at players.
- Not checked: in game only as part of the combined branch.
- In game: throw a snowball at another survival player, expect it to break on them instead of flying through; a spectator in its path is not hit.

title: fix(arrow): vanilla flight order, hit players, no per-tick packets
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

`ArrowEntity::tick` applied gravity and drag before moving. The server arrow dropped 0.05 on its first tick and ran about one tick behind the arrow the client simulates, so players saw hits on screen that the server missed, and damage used the already slowed motion. Vanilla `AbstractArrow.tick` (and 1.8) moves with the current motion first, then applies inertia, then gravity, and this now does the same. The arrow also searches targets with `get_all_at_box` and skips spectators. Before, `get_entities_at_box` left players out, so arrows never hit players. The per tick `CEntityVelocity` broadcast and the server-side crit, bubble and flame particles are gone. The client draws those trails itself (`Level.addParticle` does nothing on the server), and the entity tracker syncs the motion like `ServerEntity.sendChanges`.

Upstream #4099 also stops the server-side crit particles; this branch also drops the bubble and flame trails. The same player hit fix for the other projectiles is in {{PR:fix/projectiles-hit-players}}.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- Unit test `flight_matches_1_8_order`: a level 3 blocks/tick shot moves the full launch motion on tick 1 without dropping, then 2.97 forward and 0.05 down.
- Bot spec `40-bow.test.js` on the combined branch: the first synced arrow position is within 0.01 blocks of the 1.8 path (old binary: 0.05 low on every shot), no velocity correction packets after the spawn packet, and a full draw arrow hits a player 10 of 10 times at 8 blocks.
- Against a real 1.8.9 server (128 identical shots, legacy combat launch): level full draw shots landed 24.20 blocks away on 1.8.9, 21.04 before (13 % short) and 24.03 with this change. Flight time was 8.93 / 7.90 / 8.85 ticks, and velocity packets per flight went from 11 to 3.
- Not checked: in water, 26.3 applies the water inertia before the move, while this keeps it after the move like 1.8. The trident has its own copy of the old order and is unchanged.
- In game: shoot a player 20 or more blocks away with a full draw bow, expect the hit to register where the client shows the arrow, and no second crit trail lagging behind it.

title: fix(projectile): inherit the shooter's known movement like vanilla
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Arrows, snowballs, eggs, ender pearls, XP bottles, splash and lingering potions, tridents and wind charges flew the same whether the player stood still or sprinted. Vanilla `Projectile.shootFromRotation` adds `shooter.getKnownMovement()` (horizontal always, vertical only when the shooter is off the ground), and Pumpkin added nothing. This adds the movement of the last client position packet. It is zero when no move came in the last tick, like vanilla resets `ServerPlayer.lastKnownClientMovement` in `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleClientTickEnd`. The crossbow passes zero because `CrossbowItem.shootProjectile` uses `shoot`, and with legacy combat nothing is inherited, as in 1.8.

Builds on {{PR:feat/legacy-combat}}, whose commits are included here (it adds the `legacy_movement` field this reads); the change of this PR is the last commit.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- Bot spec `41-bow-control.test.js` on the combined branch (legacy combat off): sprinting, strafing, jumping, falling and sprint jumping shots inherit the shooter's movement, sprint shots about 1.0x the shooter velocity.
- Bot spec `40-bow.test.js` (legacy combat on): moving shots keep speed 3.0 along the look direction, nothing inherited.
- Not checked: only the bow is measured, not throwables, trident, wind charge or crossbow. Shots from a vehicle are not checked either (vanilla uses the vehicle's known movement there).
- In game: with legacy combat off, sprint forward and shoot a bow level, expect the arrow to land further than a standing shot. Strafe and throw a snowball, expect it to drift along with you. Crossbow shots stay unchanged.

title: fix(player): send the 0 health update when a player dies
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

When a Java player died, the client only got the combat kill packet (death screen). The health update with 0 never came, it only showed up with the respawn, so clients and bots that react to health (mineflayer's `death` event, mods) missed the death. `Player::handle_killed` marked the client as not loaded before calling `send_health()`, and `send_health` and `tick_health` skip clients that have not loaded. Now health is sent first (and `last_sent_health` is updated so the tick sync does not send it again), then the combat kill, then the client is marked unloaded. Vanilla `ServerPlayer.die` also marks the client unloaded (`markClientUnloadedAfterDeath`), but its health sync in `ServerPlayer.doTick` does not look at that state.

This overlaps with {{PR:fix/health-before-player-loaded}}, which lets a Java client that was loaded once get its health before `player_loaded`; this one keeps the check and only fixes the order.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- `tests/specs/70-full-game.test.js` (void kill and respawn) waits for mineflayer's `death` event, which mineflayer only emits on a health update with 0. Before the fix the void kill looked like it did nothing; on the combined branch all 60 checks pass.
- Not checked: only run on the combined branch, not on this branch alone.
- In game: die (`/kill` or the void), expect the death screen and a normal respawn; a packet log shows the health 0 update before the combat kill packet.

title: fix(text): send styled custom item names, read NBT byte booleans
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Custom item names set by plugins showed up white and italic on the client. `CustomNameImpl` was sent as `get_text()` in a plain NBT string, which drops colour, bold and `italic: false`. It now sends the full text component like `LoreImpl` next to it, as vanilla does (`DataComponents.CUSTOM_NAME` uses `ComponentSerialization.STREAM_CODEC`). Reading had a second bug: `TextComponent::from_nbt` goes through JSON, serde rejected NBT byte booleans (`bold: 1b`) and the result was an empty component, so styled names coming from the client (creative inventory) arrived empty. The boolean style fields are now read as booleans.

Upstream #3811 fixes the same name bug the same way; this was found independently. Its test, which compares against bytes from the vanilla 26.3 codec, is the second commit here.

1. fix(text): send styled custom item names; read NBT byte booleans in text components

## Description

title: fix(entity): send motion syncs to viewers only, a hit's motion once
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

In a play test, walking into another player or a shop villager felt like being punched. The push marked the player's motion dirty, and the per tick sync then sent the player its own stale server velocity (a jumping player got it too). Vanilla splits this in `ServerEntity.sendChanges`: `needsSync` motion goes to the tracking players only. The entity itself gets its motion only through `syncVelocity`, which `Entity.markHurt` sets for a hit that lands in full; it is sent once, after the tick. This does the same: `velocity_dirty` now reaches the viewers only, and a new `sync_velocity` flag carries a hit's knockback to the victim. The 1.8 melee and arrow paths send right away and clear the flag, like vanilla `Player.causeExtraKnockback`.

Builds on {{PR:feat/legacy-combat}}, whose commits are included here (its melee and arrow paths clear the new flag); the change of this PR is the last commit.

This follows the approach of upstream #3476 (vanilla `needsSync` / `syncVelocity`).

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- Bot spec `50-melee.test.js` on the combined branch: two players standing inside each other get no velocity packets for 2 s, a player inside a shop villager gets none, and the villager doesn't move. The knockback checks still get their velocity packet per hit (0.4, sprint 0.9).
- Not checked: vanilla combat mode. The specs run with legacy combat, whose hits send their own packet, so the new `sync_velocity` path for normal hits and explosions isn't covered by a spec. Bedrock isn't checked either.
- In game: walk into another player and into a villager, expect no sudden push from the server (only the small push the client does itself). Hit a mob or a player, expect knockback as before.

title: fix(net): undo a cancelled move to where the player was
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

When a plugin cancelled the `PlayerMoveEvent` of a move with rotation, the client was sent back to its old position, but once it confirmed, the server set the player to the target of the cancelled move. `handle_position_rotation` passed the cancelled target to `force_tp`, which stored it as the awaited teleport while sending the client the current position, and `handle_confirm_teleport` then applies the awaited one. Item pickup, hits, the chunk view and the viewers used the refused position while the client stood elsewhere. The cancelled branch now passes the current position, like the position-only handler already did, and `force_tp` sends the client exactly the position it awaits, as vanilla `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.teleport` does with `awaitingPositionFromClient`.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- No unit test: the move handlers need a `JavaClient`, which the crate has no test support for.
- Not checked: no bot spec cancels moves; only checked on the combined branch.
- In game: with a plugin that cancels every move, walk while turning the mouse, expect other players to keep seeing you at your old spot and no item pickup at the refused position.

title: fix(net): count a jump when the player leaves the ground, like vanilla
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

For moves with rotation, Pumpkin counted a jump when the player was on the ground before and after the move and moved up. Walking up stairs or slabs counted as jumps, while real jumps (the first packet is already off the ground) did not, which affects the jump statistic and the jump exhaustion in `Player::jump`. The check in `handle_position_rotation` now requires leaving the ground, like `handle_position` already does and like vanilla `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handlePlayerPositionChange` (`onGround() && !isOnGround && movedUpwards`).

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- Not checked: no bot spec checks jump detection; only checked on the combined branch.
- In game: walk up a staircase while turning the mouse, expect the Jumps statistic to stay the same; jump while turning, expect it to go up by one per jump.

title: fix(plugin): register the reentry scope before a blocking host operation
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

A plugin that closed players' screens at round start froze the whole server in about 1 of 15 round starts. `StoreHandle::pump_blocking` spawned the blocking operation first and registered the reentry scope after it. When the operation fired a callback right away (`close_handled_screen` fires `InventoryCloseEvent`), the callback found no scope, queued behind the guest call that was waiting for this very operation and kept the root admission, so the next `PlayerMoveEvent` on the tick thread blocked as well. The scope is now registered before `spawn_blocking`, and the pump loop moved into `pump_registered` so `pump_reentry_with_context` and `pump_blocking` share it.

Upstream #4162 makes practically the same change; this was found independently.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- `blocking_host_operation_propagates_the_reentry_chain` now also runs with a `SlowBlockingSpawner` that returns from `spawn_blocking` only after 200 ms, so the callback reaches the Store before `pump_blocking` goes on. That variant hangs without the fix (the test has a 10 s timeout).
- Not checked: no bot spec triggers the race on purpose; on the combined branch it showed in about 1 of 15 round starts after a timing change.
- In game: start many rounds with a plugin that closes open screens at round start, expect no freeze.

title: perf(tick): run small per-tick loops on the calling thread, not Rayon
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

On a 16 core host an idle server spent most of its CPU in Rayon's idle loop. Every per-tick `par_iter` over a handful of items (3 worlds, 2 players, a few dozen block entity or random ticks, natural spawning in batches of 8 chunks, the entity islands) woke the idle workers, which then spun in `sched_yield` looking for more work for longer than the work itself took (about 0.5 ms per tick). Now the worlds tick in parallel only when their ticks took 2 ms or more together on the last tick, the player, entity filter, block entity and scheduled/random tick loops only split above a minimum length (`with_min_len`, like the inhabited time loop already did), and the entity islands and natural spawning go to Rayon only after a tick in which they took 1 ms or more. Below the thresholds the order stays the same: entities tick in list order (the order the islands reproduce), and the spawning chunks are walked in their shuffled order on one thread, like vanilla `ServerChunkCache.tickChunks` does.

1. perf(tick): tick small worlds and short loops on the calling thread instead of waking Rayon
2. perf(entity): plan entity islands only when the entity ticks took >= 1 ms
3. perf(spawn): run natural spawning in order unless it took >= 1 ms on the last tick

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- New unit tests: `short_world_ticks_run_one_after_another` (2 ms world threshold, a single world never goes parallel) and `cheap_entity_ticks_are_not_planned` (no island plan on the first tick or below 1 ms, planned again at 1 ms, back to serial when the islands get cheap). `serial_schedule_retries_after_twenty_ticks_or_a_count_change` now records 1 ms of work first.
- CPU of one core over 60 s, old and new binary side by side, LAN BedWars server (3 worlds, Wasm plugin): 2 idle bots 7.6% to 1.7 to 2.7% (`RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` on the old binary: 2.0%); 2 idle bots after 4 min with leaf decay drops on the ground 6.1% to 2.0%; 1v1 round with 2 walking bots 15.8% to 5.0 to 6.0%.
- Without the plugin, mob spawning on: BedWars map with 2 idle bots 4.9% to 0.9%, 8 idle bots 5.2% to 1.4%; freshly generated world at midnight with about 120 mobs after 2.5 min 10.0% to 5.3%, with comparable spawning (59 vs 49 hostile mobs, random).
- Not checked: a busy server with many players or expensive entities (the parallel paths themselves are unchanged); measured on the BedWars fork, not on this branch alone.
- In game: start a fresh world, wait at night for 2 to 3 minutes, expect hostile mobs to spawn and move as before.

title: perf(world): hash chunk positions with Fx in the chunk maps
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

The loaded chunk map is read for every block access that goes through a chunk (light updates, random ticks, entity physics) and by the active chunk walks of each tick (random tick sampling, inhabited time, block entities). Hashing its `Vector2<i32>` key with the default SipHash was the biggest single item on the tick thread of an idle server, about 20% of its samples. The chunk position maps of `Level` (loaded chunks, entity chunks, chunk watchers, pending entity generations, chunks with scheduled ticks) and `World::block_entities` now use `FxBuildHasher` through a new `ChunkPosMap<V>` alias, like the active chunk set already does. Vanilla keys its chunk maps by the packed position in fastutil maps (for example `ChunkMap.updatingChunkMap`, a `Long2ObjectLinkedOpenHashMap`), so it does not pay for a keyed hash there either.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- LAN BedWars server, 2 idle bots after 4 min, CPU of one core over 60 s (2 runs each): 1.45 to 1.55% down to 1.35%; average tick 0.50 ms down to 0.39 to 0.48 ms. A 1v1 round with walking bots stays within the noise (4.3% vs 4.1 to 4.9%).
- Not checked: no microbenchmark; measured on the BedWars fork together with its other fixes, not on this branch alone.
- No in-game effect expected: only the hasher of the maps changes, not their contents.

title: perf(plugin): cache typed handle-event, spawn non-blocking v0.1 handlers
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Two per-event costs of the v0.1 Wasm host showed up in a BedWars round, where the plugin gets a `player-move-event` about 20 times a second per player. First, the dispatch re-typed the untyped `handle-event` Func for every event, and the type check walks the whole event variant (wasmtime `typecheck_record/variant/tuple` were about 12% of the server's samples). The handler now keeps the `TypedFunc` after its first event, through a new `typed` helper on the guest access; v0.2 already calls the generated `TypedFunc`. Second, `fire_dyn` awaits non-blocking handlers like blocking ones, so a non-blocking Wasm handler for `PlayerMoveEvent` held the tick thread for one guest call per move packet (60 to 115 µs). A non-blocking v0.1 handler cannot change the event, so `handle` now spawns the guest call as its own Tokio task and returns at once.

1. perf(plugin): type the v0.1 handle-event export once per handler instead of on every event
2. perf(plugin): a non-blocking v0.1 event handler runs as its own task instead of holding the caller

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- 1v1 round with 2 walking bots, CPU of one core over 120 s in minutes 2 to 4 of the round: 5.0% to 4.4% from the first commit.
- Bot specs on the combined branch that depend on the plugin's non-blocking `player-move-event` handler: `10-lobby.test.js` (falling below the void-kill height kills), `70-full-game.test.js` (void death within 1.5 s of dropping below the height), `60-special-items.test.js` (walking to another block cancels the Teleporter countdown).
- Not checked: event order. A spawned guest call can now run after the caller has moved on, so a plugin may see a move after the server already handled the next packet; no test covers ordering. No CPU number for the second commit alone.
- In game (with a v0.1 plugin that handles `player-move-event` non-blocking, e.g. BedWars): walk off an island into the void, expect to die right below the void-kill height as before.

title: perf(memory): trim the malloc heap once the plugins are loaded
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Compiling a Wasm plugin without a warm compile cache (the first start after a plugin update) leaves about 110 MiB of freed Cranelift buffers in glibc's main heap. glibc only returns the top of a heap to the OS by itself, so that memory stayed resident for the whole run. `init_plugins` now calls `malloc_trim(0)` once the plugins are loaded; it is compiled only for Linux with glibc, other targets are unchanged.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- LAN BedWars server with 2 idle bots: RSS with a cold plugin compile cache 361 to 243 MiB, with a warm cache 237 to 228 MiB. CPU unchanged.
- With the BedWars plugin the shifted startup timing made a deadlock in the v0.1 plugin store show up at round start (about 1 in 15); that race is fixed in {{PR:fix/plugin-reentry-scope}}, and with it 40 of 40 round starts went through.
- Not checked: other allocators and non-glibc targets (the call is not compiled there); measured on the BedWars fork, not on this branch alone.
- No in-game effect expected, only lower resident memory after startup.

title: fix(player): hand out teleport ids and queue the packet under the lock
body:
## Description

> The code and this description were written by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) while porting a LAN BedWars server to Pumpkin. The combined branch `bedwars-pvp-fixes` was play tested with real clients.

Two teleports at the same time could reach the client against their id order: the id was handed out before `awaiting_teleport` was taken and the packet was queued after it was released. The server then awaited a teleport the client had already confirmed, kicked it on the other confirm, and the client ended at the other target. `request_teleport`, `force_tp` and the dismount teleport now hand out the id, set the awaited teleport and queue the packet while holding `awaiting_teleport`, so the awaited teleport is always the last one the client gets. Vanilla `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.teleport` does these three steps together on the server thread. A dismount teleport that a newer teleport superseded (the dismount can run plugin code) is not sent any more.

Builds on {{PR:fix/teleport-chunk-view}}, {{PR:fix/move-racing-teleport}} and {{PR:fix/cancelled-move-position}}, whose commits are included here; the change of this PR is the last commit.

The lock idea is from upstream #3466 by Neol3108 (its send lock, without its queue); the single awaited teleport stays, like vanilla's `awaitingTeleport`.

## Testing

- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo test on the affected crates (CI package selection).
- Not checked: no test reproduces two concurrent teleports; only checked on the combined branch.
- In game: get teleported by a plugin in the same tick as you dismount a vehicle, expect no kick and the client at the plugin's target.
